feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 0 (60 trials, 0 completions) showed that line loss comes before every off-track failure: line_loss_events were 1.8 on the oval and 1.0 on the s-bend and slalom, and max_error sat at 0.061 to 0.064 m, just past the 0.06 m limit. That is the basis for widening the array, which you proposed. To make the wider array work I flattened the weights to be proportional to x and raised kp from 3.0 to 4.0, because the outer sensors now sit at 0.036 m and the signal per millimetre is smaller. Use the next race to decide the following steps. If line_loss_events are still above zero on the s-bend or slalom, widen the span further by trying sensor_size 0.016 with the same seven-sensor layout at 16 mm pitch (x = -0.048 to +0.048). That makes the footprints contiguous and extends the outer edge. If steering_oscillation rises above the iteration 0 level of 0.14 to 0.16 with no line loss, move the forward offset to y = 0.05 m, which is your hypothesis 2, to add phase lead and damping. If the run completes but completion_time is above 2 s, or no track completes while line loss is gone, try wheel_track 0.10 m with mass 0.6 kg (your hypotheses 3 and 4) to improve slalom turn rate and acceleration, and watch for slip.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events stay above zero on the s-bend or slalom, change sensor_size to 0.016 with seven sensors at 16 mm pitch, x = -0.048 to +0.048 and y = 0.03. Evidence: iteration 0 line loss of 1.0 to 1.8 per run on all tracks, before off-track.

If steering_oscillation rises above 0.14 to 0.16 with line_loss_events near zero, set the sensor y offset to 0.05 m (all sensors). Evidence: iteration 0 oscillation of 0.14 to 0.16, and the oval is the track most prone to jitter.

If the run completes but completion_time is above 2 s, or line loss is gone and no track completes, try wheel_track 0.10 m with mass 0.6 kg. Evidence: iteration 0 slalom had the lowest progress (0.108) and the highest rms-to-progress gap, which points to turn-rate limits.
